_about: Blind labels for docs/screen_plan_v1.md: a language model applying lab/discovery/screen_rubric.md v1 to every candidate in docs/results/screen_candidates_v1.json from its text fields alone. Written and pushed before any hand decision was opened for comparison.
labeler: a language model, in one session, one pass, no API
seen_in_docs: true when the labeler recognized the specific stone and mark from the result docs read before labeling (see the plan's blindness section); S1 is not blind (its labels are hard-coded in lab/cite_score.py)
labeling_notes: Readings of the rubric fixed during labeling, before any hand label was opened, and applied to every candidate:

1. Forward sentences: a section heading that frames its contents as the stone's consequences (reactions, response, legacy, impact, effects, aftermath, legislation, policy responses, gun control in a shooting article, memorials) counts as the record presenting the mark as a consequence; neutral sections (lead, background, production, reception) do not. Three early labels (H09, H42, H43) were revised to this reading during labeling.
2. Reverse pairs: a mark title that names the stone (a commission or an Act named for it) counts as the link even when the sentence is about something else.

3. A stated interval dates a mark when it is a quantity of time from the stone (36 hours after, within weeks, two years after, in the year after, on the second anniversary); after the release, shortly after, subsequently and has since do not.
4. A report's year dates a change only when the sentence states the change as current in that report; a study published years later about an earlier change does not.
5. Passage by both chambers (Congress passed, the Legislature passed) counts as enacted; one chamber, or an intended signing, does not.
6. Imitators and influence on later works (clones, genre conventions, competitor products, franchises) are attention_only, like adaptations.
7. A sentence cut off before it states the change does not state a mark.
8. Duplicates are judged within a set, in id order.
9. S1 (records): the mark is the bill under debate, not enacted in the sentence, so is_mark is false unless the sentence names an enacted law; the comparison for S1 is link_label.
